summary.judge:
===RULE NOTES===
1. **Adherence: still high — every rewrite is a recognizable short imperative on the same task — but the drift I flagged last round has widened, and this round's per-rewrite deltas let me price it.** The clean cases are executed well: verbose and indirect bases get decoded to canonical form, fragments get verbified ("green block on yellow block" → "Stack the green cube on the yellow cube."), and two inputs were correctly left alone. The deviations: the applier **invented attributes** again, and this time wrongly — "Grab that red aluminum can and set it on the plate." became "...place it on the **green** plate." (the coke-task plate is yellow in the evidence bank; green is the *carrot*-task's plate — cross-task contamination), and "that spoon" became "the **green** spoon" (the bank calls it metal/silver). It **mutated a spatial relation** again — "Transfer the carrot over to the wheel." → "Put the carrot **in the center of** the wheel.", the second straight round the wheel relation got embellished — and invented "toy wheel" in another rewrite. It **flipped verbs on already-clean inputs** four times (place→put twice, stack→put, put→stack), directionless churn the rule never asked for. Its no-op policy is inconsistent: one clean input passed through byte-identical and uncapitalized while its twin got capitalized, and one output ("put the red can in the white bowl standing vertical") isn't a plain imperative at all.

   **Performance: the book measured +0.049 (0.278 with rules vs 0.229 unrephrased), positive but roughly half of last round's +0.083 draw.** The 40 scored samples: 13 wins, 9 losses, 18 ties, net +150 points on the 0–100 rollout scale (mean +3.75 per sample). Deltas are quantized at 16.667 — one rollout in six — and a capitalization-and-period-only rewrite swung −16.7, so any single ±16.7 is noise-adjacent; I weight the patterns, not the individual flips. The pattern is stark. **Every large win is on a degraded input**: the verbose ramekin instruction +66.7, the fragment +50, "the yellow one" resolved to "the yellow cube" +33.3, the verbose spoon instruction +33.3, and eight +16.7s almost all on verbose/adversarial bases. **The losses are almost all self-inflicted on inputs that were already fine**: the −50 was a synonym swap ("standing up"→"upright") on a clean natural, the −33.3 was the hallucinated green plate, −16.7s came from the green spoon, from dropping words out of a 66.7-scoring base, and from three of the four verb flips. Summed crudely: rewriting degraded inputs earned ~+300 of the +350 gross gain, while touching clean inputs plus inventing attributes accounts for ~−150 of the −200 gross loss. The rule as written cannot tell these apart because it fires unconditionally.

   **What to do: keep the rule as the book's core — it is clearly net-positive where it belongs — and split it into a fire condition plus guardrails.** Concretely, replace it with: *"If the instruction is verbose, indirect, polite, a fragment, or names objects by paraphrase, rewrite it as a short plain imperative naming the objects plainly; otherwise leave it unchanged."* and a second rule: *"Keep the original verb when it is already a common manipulation verb, keep the exact spatial relation (on/in/into), and never add a color, size, or material the instruction did not mention."* The attribute ban is the strongest-evidenced change this round: the bank shows *correct* scene colors help a lot (black keyboard, blue towel, orange carrot on black wheel), but the applier demonstrably does not know the scene — it guessed green for a yellow plate and green for a silver spoon — so at rewrite time, with no scene access, guessing is strictly downside; the clause earns its way back only if the rewriter is ever given scene metadata to ground the color. The no-op guard is next best evidenced (seven of nine losses were rewrites of clean inputs) but is confounded with rollout noise at n=6, so I would want the controlled measurement: run the guarded book against the current book on the same eval — that one comparison settles whether the guard's ~−100 points of avoided churn is real. The verb-preservation clause costs nothing and removes four coin-flips. Do not add a capitalization/punctuation clause in either direction: the identical-pass-through, the capitalized twin, and the formatting-only −16.7 together say formatting is inside the noise floor, and both rounds of bank evidence agree.

===SUGGESTIONS===
Measure "put the coke can on the green plate" on the coke-on-plate task against the well-measured "put the coke can on the plate" — prices the wrong-color penalty the applier actually incurred (−33.3 in this sample) and decides how hard the attribute ban should be worded.
Measure "put the green spoon on the towel" against "put the spoon on the towel" — same question on the manipulated object rather than the target; tells us whether object-side hallucination is as costly as target-side.
Measure "put the carrot in the center of the wheel" against "put the carrot on the wheel" — prices the relation embellishment the applier has now produced two rounds running on the hardest task.
Measure "put the carrot on the toy wheel" — the applier invented "toy" and gained +16.7 (one rollout); the bank shows real modifiers ("black") help on this task, so this tells us whether novel non-color modifiers are a hidden win or noise.
Re-measure "put the coke can in the ramekin" (still only n=12 in the bank) against the dense "put the coke can in the white bowl" — the ramekin-vs-bowl canonicalization direction is still unsettled and the applier keeps translating to "white bowl" on faith.
